newsitem.title: CANADA: Seagram jumps on "Lost World" opening.
newsitem.headline: Seagram jumps on "Lost World" opening.

text.p: Shares of Seagram Co Ltd surged on Canadian exchanges on Monday, powered by a record-breaking opening weekend for Steven Spielberg's "The Lost World", traders said.

"This ought to become a fairly strong money maker for Universal, which is Seagram's," said Fred Ketchen, director of equity trading for Scotia McLeod Inc. "When they (investors) see something like this happen, you've got to translate that into the company's stock."
Seagram shares reached a three-month high in Toronto and Montreal after reports that the "Jurassic Park" sequel earned US$90.1 million over the weekend, according to studio estimates.
"The Lost World" was released by Universal Pictures, which is 80 percent-owned by Seagram.

Shares of the Montreal-based beverage and entertainment company jumped 1 to 56.20 in late afternoon trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange and by 1.10 to 56.20 on the Montreal Exchange. Seagram shares did not trade on Wall Street for the Memorial Day holiday.
"The Lost World" broke the previous Memorial Day opening weekend record held by "Mission: Impossible" and bettered Universal's estimates, according to a studio spokesman.
The film has a reported budget of US$80 million, well below most of the summer's major releases such as "Men In Black" and "Titanic".
